text:
elyse: quick heads-up — i pushed a prototype for deferred KV-cache hydration (branch: deferred-kv). It streams safetensors shards and continues serving while a background worker hydrates layer kvs. Needs API for consumers to know hydration progress. any strong objections?

devin: interesting. primary concern is eviction interplay — if background hydrates but evictor runs it could thrash. do we want a hint that pins recently-hydrated layers? :thinking: 

raj_k: agree on eviction. also encryption headers complicate head-first streaming. If header decrypts late, background hydrate may stall. We should add a small manifest field indicating "decrypt_priority" and fallback behavior.

maria: i think we need two surfaces: 1) loader-level events (hydration_started/hydration_done/error) for observability and 2) a tiny query API for apps to poll hydration_state per-layer. Example idea: `GET /v1/weights/:model/hydration_state?layer=attn.kv` returns `{state: "hydrating|ready|failed", progress: 0..100}`. keep it lightweight.

elyse: that matches my thinking. prototype currently emits loader events to the runtime event bus, but there's no stable HTTP query. we should define semantics: "ready" means layer present in local KV cache and pinned for X seconds? or simply present in memory?

devin: prefer conservative: "ready" = mapped in process address space (can't be evicted for Y ms) so caller can safely issue low-latency requests. we can make pin-time configurable via policy.

raj_k: +1. also propose `warmup_hints` in model manifest for long-running jobs so loader can prioritize layers required for short prompts. small example: 
```json
"warmup_hints": {
  "layers": ["attn.kv", "feed_forward.0"],
  "priority": "background",
  "pin_ms": 2000
}
```
This would let runtime prioritize and temporarily pin hydrated layers.

maria: we should record telemetry: time_to_ready per-layer, hydration_cpu_ms, bytes_transferred, and a failure_code if decrypt/verify fails. hook these into Console so devs can set alerts (e.g., regression when attn.kv > 300ms).

loader-bot: CI: deferred-kv prototype test matrix passed 12/14. failing cases: encrypted-header path (timeout flake).

elyse: noted. fallback plan in prototype currently retries decrypt then falls back to blocking hotload for that shard. that's what caused the flake. we can instead expose `hydratable=false` in manifest for shards requiring blocking decrypt by default.

devin: question on API ergonomics: do we want a push callback (webhook/event subscription) for hydration events or keep it pull-based (polling)? push feels nicer but adds infra complexity.

raj_k: push would be great for Dedicated customers who want deterministic rollouts. For Hosted API, polling + events for power users might be enough. maybe support both but with low-fidelity default events (sampler) to avoid noise.

maria: +1 to both. define minimal event envelope now so we can iterate: `{model, shard_id, layer, state, ts, progress, failure_code?}`. keep payload small.

elyse: action items: 1) i'll open an RFC PR describing `hydration_state` query API + minimal event envelope (owner: elyse) 2) raj_k to draft manifest additions (`warmup_hints`, `decrypt_priority`, `hydratable`) 3) devin to sketch eviction pin semantics & config knobs 4) maria to enumerate telemetry metrics and alert suggestions. target: 2 weeks for RFC + proto fixes.

devin: ack, i'll add a short design doc for pin_ms semantics and eviction priority.

raj_k: ack, will draft manifest schema. i'll also add a compatibility note: loader should tolerate unknown `warmup_hints`.

maria: i'll stub Console alerts and a sample dashboard panel.

elyse: one more note — please avoid coupling hydration readiness to model version rollout. hydration_state must be per-running instance and not globally interpreted as "model ready". we'll clarify in RFC. :+1:

devin: :thumbsup:
